chapter: San Francisco, the So Different Orchestra and Johnny
title: Johnny's blindness, his teaching studio and the Spikes music store
summary: Johnny's eye operation left him nearly blind; later he taught piano and band instruments in the music store, rehearsing his students' bands there.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Learning your horn: teachers, lessons and fees

blocks.x: Oh, I told you he went blind, and I used to have to lead him on the stage around. I'd lead him from instrument to instrument, and then he had a operation, and they put him on the table, and this operation, and they went down in there, and, of course, they didn't know much about eye operations those days, and they just cut out a piece of his eyeball--what do you call that?--and they cut it like it was a "V". It wasn't round. And he could see for...uh... and after that, he had to put his music up real close like this when he played the piano, he'd put it up and play it like this, and when we did the musical act and everything, he would stick close to me and... uh, he knew where the instruments were but he didn't know how close or, you know, he knew the position they's always in, so we'd walk from instrument to instrument but he...I'd be guiding him, you know. And then, when he come home, he started a school, after he got home, after we had the music store. I ran the music store, and he opened

in the morning or something while I sleep, and if I was out playing that night, my sister would open the music store, and that went on for three or four years, and he had his school, and he had a couple of girl bands and a men's band, and he taught 'em all and everything in his school and everything.
What was the name of his school?

Well, he didn't have no name. He was just a music teacher but he had all these scholars and things, and he taught them, you know, instrument by instrument, he taught 'em piano and saxophone and clarinet and drums and trumpet. That's about all he taught 'em, I think, and a lot of them come to him that already knew how to play 'cause he had a studio, and ever...twice...once or twice a week, he'd have his band rehearsals, so that, if you was one of his students, and I was your friend, you'd say, "Come on up and play with us," you know, and that way, he had his band. So this band was organized in our music store. That's how we got together with this band. You see Paul Howard on there?
